strat.cruxMap:
PRECISE CRUX MAP of the LRC(14) true-wide region (REGION III: second-largest(E)>14, base B bounded, >=2 far speeds).

(1) THE RECURSION SPINE (one-far -> two-far). PROVED one-far (THM-546/547): peel w=max(E), E'=E\{w}; p0(E)=Phi(E')+Delta_w EXACTLY, Phi(E')=p0(E')+(1/7)p1(E') (plateau), |Delta_w|<=(6/49)V(E')/w with sup|F_j|=3/49 (centered sawtooth antiderivative; VERIFIED rational). This closes max<=14 (kps-S19) and the boundary collar 2nd-largest<=14 (THM-547, modulo a feasible-but-unrun finite check 14<w<=w*, w*=54/90/103). REGION III is where E' itself is wide so V(E')~spread is UNBOUNDED and the one-far bound is vacuous (O(1) at w~max). That is the whole reason the two-far object is needed.

(2) THE TWO-FAR CURVATURE I_B(u,v)=p0(B u {u,v})-p0(B u {u})-p0(B u {v})+p0(B) (mixed 2nd difference; symmetric; order-independent endpoint). EXACT decomposition (THM-548, file lines 28-32, I re-derived/verified): with A_j={x: B misses exactly sector j}, A_{jj'}={x: B misses exactly {j,j'}}, p1=Sum_j meas(A_j), p2=Sum_{j<j'} meas(A_{jj'}),
   I_B(u,v) = -Sum_j INT 1_{A_j} 1_j(ux)1_j(vv) + Sum_{j<j'} INT 1_{A_{jj'}}[1_j(ux)1_{j'}(vx)+1_{j'}(ux)1_j(vx)].
Reading: ONE far runner fills <=1 missed sector (one-far peel acts on A_j, p1); TWO far runners can JOINTLY rescue the exactly-two-missed strata A_{jj'} (one each into j,j') — this is the genuinely new second-order mass, exactly the A_{jj'} channel that one-far cannot see.

(3) THE DECORRELATED LIMIT Phi_2(B)=(2 p2(B)-p1(B))/49 (COMPUTED+VERIFIED EXACTLY: on HYP-2675 core B=(0,4,6,8,10,12,14) I confirmed p1=601/1470, p2=19/84, Phi_2=32/36015=0.000889). As u,v->infinity independently (2-D Weyl), each joint sector indicator decorrelates to 1/49 (=(1/7)^2): the negative A_j-channel loses (1/49)p1, the positive A_{jj'}-channel gains 2/49 per missed pair -> (2 p2 - p1)/49. PROVED status: the LIMIT formula is exact arithmetic (verified); the CLAIM that it is the genuine 2-D Weyl limit is a clean equidistribution statement (high confidence, standard).

(4) THE DEVIATION = RESONANCE (THE CRUX). Fourier-expand 1_j(y)=Sum_m shat_j(m)e(my):
   I_B(u,v) - Phi_2(B) = Sum_{j,j'}(+-) Sum_{(m,n)!=(0,0)} shat_j(m) shat_{j'}(n) * 1hat_{A_.}(-(mu+nv)).
The CONTROLLING FREQUENCY is the RESONANCE L=mu+nv. shat_j(m)=e(-mj/7)(1-e(-m/7))/(2 pi i m), |shat_j(m)|=|sin(pi m/7)|/(pi|m|), shat_j(7m)=0 (THM-503 apex-prime vanishing thins BOTH frequencies in the product). 1hat_A(L) has BV decay |1hat_A(L)|<=#arcs(A)/(pi|L|). So the deviation is a DOUBLE Fourier sum whose every term is gated by 1/|mu+nv|.

(5) THE RESONANCE/DEVIATION SPLIT (the dichotomy). NON-RESONANT: if u,v have no small additive relation, |mu+nv| is large for all small (m,n) -> deviation ->0 by BV decay (VERIFIED numerically: B=(0,4,6,8,10,12,14), dev shrinks 15,17->0.0104, 31,47->0.0014, 200,401->0.0005 as the pair grows/desonates). RESONANT: small (m,n) with mu+nv=O(1) <=> u/v ~ -n/m <=> a short relation between the two far runners <=> u,v lie in a common low-dim GAP with B <=> Freiman structure <=> boundary-function "ambiguous/shared-asymptotic-direction" point. On resonance THM-531 scale-invariance reduces the pair to a BOUNDED model (finite check).

(6) WHERE THE RELATION LATTICE / FREIMAN ENTERS. The resonance set is exactly the additive-combinatorial structured set: covolume(Lambda°(E))=|e/gcd(e)|_2 (PROVED, HYP-2606 F1); AP uniquely minimizes covolume AND lambda_1 (PROVED) — the densest/most-resonant relations. Freiman dimension d organizes the survivors: d=1 (dilated/translated AP) -> THM-531 collapses to bounded finite check; d>=2 -> longer shortest relation -> dimension penalty (HYP-2637, VERIFIED ~0.5x per dim, margin>=0.21 at k=8). CRITICAL EMPIRICAL CORRECTION (codex S50 atlas, VERIFIED): the actual k=9 direct-risk LEADER (0,4,6,8,10,12,14,15,16), p0=321/980, margin 11681/70070, has NEGATIVE curvature I_B(15,16)=-13/1470 (I re-verified the exact Fraction), and its core is 2*(0,2,3,4,5,6,7) — a gcd(core)=2 DILATED-CORE d=1 row, NOT a positive two-far synergy. Largest-positive row (0,1,4,8,10,12,14,16,20) has I_B=307/1960 but is SAFE (p0=89/336, verified). So HYP-2679's literal premise ("true-wide leaders have large positive curvature") is REFUTED; the true picture is: the cap-threatening true-wide rows are d=1 dilated-core rows handled by scale-invariance, and positive curvature is real but sub-critical.
strat.boundaryFramework:
THE BOUNDARY-FUNCTION FRAMEWORK MADE PRECISE FOR LRC.

THE EXPLICIT DICTIONARY (fixed, with the metric/measure caveat made explicit):
- Boundary point x on circle C  <->  fixed bounded CORE B subset {0,...,14} (the boundary datum / state word).
- Radial approach z->x in disk D  <->  a single far speed w->infinity. A SEQUENCE/curve of far speeds  <->  an APPROACH ARC.
- f(z) (disk function)  <->  the exact coverage functional p0(E), E=B u F. (Carry the pair (p0,p1) or (p0,p1,p2) as the M-valued datum.)
- Curvilinear limit p along arc gamma  <->  the decorrelated w->infinity plateau lim_w p0(B u {w}) = Phi(B)=p0(B)+(1/7)p1(B).
- BOUNDARY FUNCTION phi: B |-> Phi(B)  <->  the plateau map. The one-far curvilinear limit EXISTS exactly: Delta_w=p0(B u {w})-Phi(B), |Delta_w|<=(6/49)V(B)/w -> 0 (PROVED). This IS "the curvilinear/radial limit at the boundary point B exists and equals phi(B)."
- AMBIGUOUS POINT (two arcs, two limits)  <->  a (B,u,v) where two DIFFERENT far-approach arcs give different iterated limits. For ONE far runner the plateau is unique (never ambiguous, since p0 is order-independent). Ambiguity is a TWO-FAR phenomenon: the two-far curvature I_B(u,v) IS the AMBIGUITY DEFECT / second mixed difference; nonzero arc-DEPENDENT I_B = curvilinear ambiguity in true-wide. Resonance mu+nv~0 = two arcs along a shared asymptotic (rationally-related) direction = a Bagemihl ambiguous point.

WHICH BOUNDARY-FUNCTION THEOREMS BECOME USABLE TOOLS, AND HOW (qualitative shape, NOT the quantitative inequality):

1. BAGEMIHL ambiguous-point theorem (the set of ambiguous points of ANY f is at most COUNTABLE; sharp). USE: it is the TARGET-SHAPE engine. It justifies AIMING to prove the set of true-wide (B,u,v) with large arc-dependent I_B is finite/low-rank/structured (the d=1 scale-invariant family per THM-531 + a finite base check) rather than a positive-density obstruction. It is the moral reason the resonant exceptional set SHOULD be thin. CAVEAT (flagged): Bagemihl gives countability for VALUE-ambiguity; LRC resonance is CURVATURE(derivative)-ambiguity, and w*Delta_w is PERIODIC in w (rational breakpoints) so resonances recur with positive density ALONG the w-axis. So the right exceptional object is (cores/far-pairs), not (core,w) triples — the transfer is an analogy, not a literal theorem, until an ambient measure on far-pairs (u,v) is fixed.

2. McMILLAN F_sigma_delta + honorary-Baire-2 (boundary function of a continuous f is Baire-1 off a countable set; convergence set is F_sigma_delta). USE: justifies the bounded-vs-wide SPLIT THM-547 already exploits: a SMALL exceptional set (bounded near-AP cores, the finite check) + an F_sigma_delta "good" bulk (wide cores) where the plateau bound is clean. Matches the data: only bounded consec/near-AP cores are tight; ALL wide cores have p0<=~0.223<<cap_9 (margin>=0.27).

3. FATOU nontangential vs tangential + PLESSNER (mes E=0). USE: the VALUE-vs-PATH split. p0 is the Fatou a.e. object (order-independent endpoint, well-defined, below cap with margin >=0.27 a.e.); Delta_w/I_B is the path-DERIVATIVE/curvature where resonance "tangentially" diverges. Plessner is the cleanest "bad set has measure zero" template: assert the resonant cores form a density-zero family relative to all wide cores. This LEGITIMIZES bounding via the order-independent p0, not the raw arc derivative.

4. BAGEMIHL-PIRANIAN "+1 Baire class" (boundary of Baire-xi is Baire-(xi+1)). USE: each far-runner peel in the recursion costs at most ONE regularity level, so iterating the plateau recursion (peel max repeatedly) cannot generate pathology — the limit object stays mildly-above-finite. Caps descriptive complexity of the multi-far (>2) limit.

5. COLLINGWOOD maximality/symmetry (curvilinear != full cluster set is first category; two-arc cluster sets coincide residually). USE: the category-side genericity companion — generic (non-arithmetically-commensurate) far pairs have symmetric small curvature; only meager lcm-resonant cores deviate. Pairs with the measure-side Plessner statement.

6. TOPOLOGICAL DEGREE / bidegree on T^2 (Report 7). The two-far map Phi(x)=(frac(ux),frac(vx)):[0,1)->T^2 is a line of homology class (u,v) in H_1(T^2)=Z^2; I_B(u,v) is the SIGNED algebraic intersection number of this (u,v)-line with the two coordinate danger-bands, O(1) per cell iff the relation lattice of {B,u,v} has bounded covolume (Diophantine regime), commensurate-large for dilated-AP cores, small/negative when (u,v) adds a fresh lattice dimension. This is the topological MAKE-PRECISE of "resonance = small mu+nv": the intersection number is governed by gcd(u,v) and the continued fraction of v/u (three-gap -> five-gap dichotomy, arXiv 2009.08444).

NET: the boundary-function literature supplies the STRUCTURE/target-shape (small structured exceptional set + F_sigma_delta good bulk + bounded Baire complexity + intersection-number invariant), telling the prover WHERE the resonant set lives and that it SHOULD be thin/structured. It does NOT supply the quantitative inequality (HYP-2655 already refuted any uniform constant C<=1.95; C>=3.91 at multiscale resonances) — that must come from the signed double-Abel bound + Freiman reduction below.
strat.proofStrategy:
CONCRETE STEP-BY-STEP STRATEGY FOR THM-548 AND TRUE-WIDE CLOSURE.

PART A — THE EXACT DEVIATION FORM (foundation, mostly done).
A1. Confirm the exact integral identity for I_B (THM-548 lines 28-32) by the same inclusion-exclusion that gave the one-far peel: one far runner acts on A_j (exactly-one-missed), two far runners jointly act on A_{jj'} (exactly-two-missed). Re-derive p0(B u {u,v}) - (the two one-far peels) + p0(B) and check the A_{jj'} cross-terms appear with the stated signs. [The leader value I_B(15,16)=-13/1470 and largest-pos 307/1960 are already exactly verified, so the object is correct.]
A2. Establish Phi_2=(2p2-p1)/49 as the genuine 2-D Weyl limit: u,v jointly equidistribute on T^2 when {u,v} dissociated; each joint indicator 1_j(ux)1_{j'}(vx) -> (1/7)(1/7). [Limit arithmetic VERIFIED exactly; the equidistribution step is standard.]
A3. Write the deviation double-Fourier sum I_B-Phi_2 = Sum_{j,j'}(+-) Sum_{(m,n)!=(0,0)} shat_j(m)shat_{j'}(n) 1hat_{A}(-(mu+nv)), with the apex-prime vanishing shat_j(7m)=0 on both factors.

PART B — THE NON-RESONANT ANALYTIC BOUND (the new analytic content).
B1. SECOND-ABEL (double sawtooth). Sum in m and n FIRST (as the one-far Abel summed in n first to get F_j with sup=3/49). The two-far analogue is a SECOND antiderivative G_j = centered antiderivative of F_j. I VERIFIED G_j is rationally bounded (node values up to 5/686=0.00729; the true sup is on a segment interior but is an exact rational from the piecewise-quadratic vertices — compute it exactly with a supG_exact routine analogous to supF_exact). This yields a bound |I_B-Phi_2| <= C_2 * (arc-interaction count) / dist((u,v), resonance lattice), where C_2 is the explicit rational curvature constant (the parabolic analogue of 6/49) and dist is measured by min over small (m,n) of |mu+nv|.
B2. QR REALITY for the product. The product shat_j(m)shat_{j'}(n) is REAL under the JOINT (m,n)<->(-m,-n) pairing by the SAME 6=-1 non-residue mod 7 argument (D7(-c)=conj(D7(c))) — gives a real, signable two-far deviation, licensing the signed/Abel form. [VERIFY this extends to the product; Report 1 flags it as conjectural-but-expected.]
B3. ERDOS-TURAN/KOKSMA head+tail split on the double sum: cut at |m|,|n|<=M; head is a finite signed sum estimated by the second-Abel sup; tail <= (V/pi^2)(1/M) per axis. Off resonance the head's 1/|mu+nv| factor is uniformly small -> total deviation O(1/dist), hence I_B-Phi_2 -> 0 with an EXPLICIT rate.
B4. Conclude: for non-resonant (B,u,v), p0(B u {u,v}) = p0(B) + [two one-far peels, bounded by THM-547 over bounded B] + Phi_2(B) + (small deviation). Since Phi_2 is a finite-base quantity (bounded B) and the one-far peels are THM-547-controlled, p0 <= cap_k with margin. [Data supports: non-resonant pairs decay to ~0; all wide cores p0<=0.223.]

PART C — THE RESONANT REDUCTION (Freiman/scale-invariance).
C1. DEFINE resonance precisely: (u,v) is resonant for B if there exist small (m,n) (height <= H0, an explicit cutoff from the cap margin) with mu+nv=O(1). Equivalently {B,u,v} has covolume below a threshold / sits in a Freiman GAP of dim d.
C2. d=1 (dilated/translated AP, e.g. the actual leader core 2*(0,2,3,4,5,6,7)): apply THM-531 scale-invariance (x->frac(dx) measure-preserving, translation = rigid rotation) to collapse the dilated AP to its bounded consecutive model -> the row reduces EXACTLY to a bounded finite check already covered by kps-S19/THM-547. The atlas confirms the unique direct-risk champion lives in the gcd(core)=2 dilated bank — this is the d=1 route.
C3. d>=2 (genuine higher-dim GAP): use the dimension penalty (HYP-2637, ~0.5x per dimension, VERIFIED) to show Phi_2 and the resonant deviation are both bounded well below cap; positive curvature can occur but direct risk is sub-critical (largest-pos row p0=89/336 < leader). NEEDED: the SIGNED magnitude bound for the d>=2 relation lattice (HYP-2678 part 3, OPEN) — the only genuinely missing analytic piece; an absolute bound is PROVED 5x too lossy (HYP-2606 F3), so it must keep (-1)^|T| and the 7-vanishing (Poisson/theta).

PART D — ASSEMBLY (true-wide closure).
D1. Finite resonance lattice: for bounded B and the cap margin, only finitely many resonance directions -n/m (small height) matter -> finitely many resonant families, each d=1 (scale-reduced to finite check) or d>=2 (dimension-penalty bounded). This is the Bagemihl-countable / finite-curvature-ledger target made effective.
D2. Off all resonances: Part B analytic bound. The union covers all true-wide (B,u,v).
D3. Iterate for >=3 far speeds: peel the largest far runner, reducing m-far to (m-1)-far over a base that now includes one fewer far speed; the "+1 Baire class" cap guarantees no complexity blow-up. Each peel is one approach-arc step.

WHAT MUST BE COMPUTED/VERIFIED: (i) the exact rational curvature constant C_2 = sup|G_j| (second antiderivative) in Fraction arithmetic; (ii) the QR-reality of the product kernel; (iii) the explicit resonance cutoff H0 from the cap_k margins; (iv) exhaustive (not spot) confirmation that the d=1 dilated-core reduction lands inside the existing finite check; (v) the signed d>=2 bound. THM-548 status: limit PROVED (verified), deviation Fourier form derived, non-resonant Abel bound = the deliverable to write, resonant reduction = assembly of existing PROVED tools (THM-531) + one OPEN piece (signed d>=2).
nextComputations: Exact supG_exact: compute the second-antiderivative curvature constant C_2 = sup_y|G_j(y)| in Fraction arithmetic (G_j = centered antiderivative of F_j), over segment interiors of the piecewise-quadratic, for all j=1..6 — the parabolic analogue of sup|F_j|=3/49. I found node values up to 5/686 but the true sup is on a segment interior; pin the exact rational. This is the constant in the non-resonant two-far Abel bound.

QR-reality of the product kernel: verify in Z[zeta_7] that shat_j(m)shat_{j'}(n) is real under the joint (m,n)<->(-m,-n) pairing (D7 product version of 6=-1 non-residue), confirming the signed two-far deviation is licit (Report 1 flags this as expected-but-undemonstrated).

Resonance-vs-deviation exact scan: for B=(0,4,6,8,10,12,14) and a grid of far pairs (u,v) up to ~600, tabulate exact I_B-Phi_2 against min over small (m,n) (height<=6) of |mu+nv|; fit the decay to C_2*V/|mu+nv| and confirm the BV/Abel rate and the explicit resonance cutoff H0.

Double Erdos-Turan/Koksma head+tail: extend signed_erdos_turan to the 2-D sum Sum_{(m,n)} shat_j(m)shat_{j'}(n)1hat_A(-(mu+nv)); measure head (|m|,|n|<=M) vs tail and the empirical sharpening factor below the absolute double bound.

Resonance-divergence stress test: confirm whether the two-far deviation sum can DIVERGE at a stacked multiscale resonant pair (analogue of the {0,1,2,30,31,32,60,61} resonance-stacking that gave sup w|Delta_w|=5.196); check the offsetting plateau Phi_2 stays small so p0<=cap survives even when the raw deviation grows.

d=1 dilated-core finite-check verification: for every gcd(core)=2 (and gcd>=2) true-wide row in the k=9 atlas, apply THM-531 scale-reduction explicitly and confirm the reduced bounded row is inside the kps-S19/THM-547 finite check (the atlas shows the unique champion lives here — make it a closed reduction, not just an observation).

Signed d>=2 magnitude bound prototype: implement a Poisson/theta signed sum over the d>=2 relation lattice (keeping (-1)^|T| and shat_j(7m)=0) and test whether it beats the cap margin on the largest-positive-curvature rows (e.g. (0,1,4,8,10,12,14,16,20), I_B=307/1960) — the one OPEN analytic piece.

Exhaustively run the THM-547 collar finite check 14<w<=w* (w*=54/90/103) that is currently only spot-verified, and re-run with the exact cap_10=55/91 instead of the conservative floor 4/7 to recover the true margin.
risks: DIVERGENT RESONANCE SUM: the deviation double-Fourier sum is gated by 1/|mu+nv|; at stacked multiscale resonances (resonance-stacking, VERIFIED sup grows 0.730->2.542->3.909->5.196 with #scales) the controlling frequency hits ~0 for MULTIPLE small (m,n) simultaneously, so the per-term 1/|mu+nv| does not give a uniform constant — HYP-2655 already REFUTED any uniform C<=1.95 (C>=3.91). The non-resonant Abel bound only works strictly off resonance; closure depends on the OFFSETTING small plateau (Phi_2 and base p0 are tiny for wide B), which is computational not yet analytic. Risk: the joint plateau/deviation recursion (HYP-2655 sec.4) is unproven.

EXCEPTIONAL SET NOT STRUCTURED: the boundary-function transfer (Bagemihl countable, Plessner null) is an ANALOGY, not a literal theorem — no ambient measure on the space of cores/far-pairs is fixed, so 'countable/measure-zero' is not yet meaningful. Worse, w*Delta_w is PERIODIC in w, so resonances recur with POSITIVE DENSITY along w; if the right exceptional object turns out to be (core,w) triples rather than (core) or (far-pair), it is NOT thin and the Bagemihl target shape fails.

SIGNED d>=2 BOUND MISSING (the genuine open gap): an absolute geometry-of-numbers bound is PROVED 5-6x too lossy (HYP-2606 F3, AbsTrue(AP)=1.773 >> margin 0.357); the smallness is intra-support SIGNED cancellation growing 10-80x at support 4-7. The required signed (Poisson/theta) magnitude bound for the d>=2 relation lattice is NOT written. HYP-2662 further refuted the naive QR/trace route (intra-quadratic residual dominates). Without it, the resonant d>=2 branch is unclosed.

HYP-2679 LITERAL PREMISE IS FALSE: the actual k=9 leader (0,4,6,8,10,12,14,15,16) has NEGATIVE curvature -13/1470, NOT 'large positive' (VERIFIED). The whole 'true-wide leaders = positive-curvature exceptions' framing is wrong; the live obstruction is d=1 dilated-core overlap rows. If the strategy keys on positive curvature it targets the wrong objects — the correct route is scale-invariance on dilated cores, which is the SAFE/known route, so positive curvature may be a red herring that consumes effort.

QR-REALITY MAY NOT EXTEND TO THE PRODUCT: the signed/Abel collapse for one-far relies on Delta_w being real (6=-1 NQR pairing). For the product shat_j(m)shat_{j'}(n) the joint pairing is ASSERTED to work but UNVERIFIED (Report 1 flags 'conjectural, not demonstrated'). If reality fails for the product, the second-Abel sawtooth/parabola collapse and the rational constant C_2 are not licensed, and only the (loose) absolute double bound survives.

FINITE CHECKS UNRUN / CAPS LOOSE: THM-547's collar check 14<w<=w* (~2.6e5 clusters at k=9) is only spot-verified; cap_10 uses the conservative floor 4/7 not the exact 55/91. The d=1 reduction in Part C2 is an atlas OBSERVATION not a proved closed reduction. Region III closure is 'reduction proved modulo computation' at best, and the upstream glue (HYP-2603 consec-maximizes, integer-vs-real passage) is still assumed — LRC(14) remains NOT proved.
